newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank rates held steady, assets statement due.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank rates held steady, assets statement due.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Wednesday its council had agreed to leave the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.
The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was also held steady at three percent.
The central bank also announced that it would make a further statement later in the afternoon on plans by the Bonn government to revalue the central bank's assets.
The fortnightly council meeting was held a day earlier than usual due to Thursday's regional German holiday.

Few economists had expected a change in rates at the meeting, with discussions expected to focus on Bonn's plans to revalue the German central bank's assets in a bid to shore up finances and meet entry criteria for the new European currency.

"A statement from the central bank council on the concept presented by the finance ministry with regard to the accounting systems of the German Bundesbank is likely to be released in the course of the later afternoon," the central bank said.

Government sources said on Tuesday the central bank was expected to approve the revaluation of its gold reserves that could swell German federal finances by up to 12 billion marks in 1997 and to also issue a statement after the meeting.

But Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer was reported in an unconfirmed newspaper article on Wednesday as having warned Bonn two months ago that any such revaluation in the run-up to EMU risked damaging Germany's credibility.
The Bundesbank has about 95 million ounces of gold valued in its books at well below current market levels.

Any revenues raised would be a possible lifeline to Waigel, who presented the controversial plan to the Bundesbank council two weeks ago, due to an estimated 18 billion mark shortfall in 1997 tax revenues announced earlier this month.
